title: Biryaani
author: Chef Amina Hassan
desc: Chicken marinated overnight in a green paste of ginger, garlic, mint, cilantro and freshly ground spice, grilled half-done, then layered with fried onions, part-cooked rice and saffron and steamed sealed in the oven.
longDesc: The Somali approach to biryani solves the problem every biryani cook knows — rice and meat that want different amounts of time. Here the chicken is grilled to halfway, the rice boiled to six minutes, the vegetables cooked separately, and everything finishes together under foil. Nothing is left to guesswork, which is why Somali cooks pass this method around rather than the all-in-one version.
ingredients: Canola oil, 5 cm deep, for frying the onions
1 tsp saffron threads, steeped in 80 ml hot water
1/2 tsp rose water or kewra water (optional)
equipment: Deep baking dish and aluminium foil
steps: Grind the coriander, cumin, cardamom, peppercorns, cloves and bay leaves to a fine powder.
Blend the ginger, garlic, cilantro, mint and chillies to a paste in a food processor.
Mix the paste with the ground spices, turmeric, bouillon powder and the 120 ml oil, rub it all over the chicken, cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours and preferably overnight.
Soak the rice in the 1.5 L of water for 1 hour.
Slice the onions and fry them in batches over medium heat until deep golden. Drain and reserve.
Shake the excess marinade off the chicken, keeping it, and grill or broil the chicken at 204C / 400F for 15 minutes — it should be only half cooked.

Heat the 2 tbsp oil in a pan, add the reserved marinade and fry for a minute. Add the tomato and potato and stir, then the yogurt and bouillon powder. Cover and cook on low for 30 minutes, until the potato yields to a fork.
Steep the saffron in the hot water.

Bring the 3 L of water to a hard boil with the salt, bay leaves, cumin seeds and 2 tbsp oil. Drain the soaked rice, add it and boil for exactly 6 minutes. Lift it out with a slotted spoon while it is still hot and very moist — do not drain it dry.
In a deep baking dish, lay the chicken, scatter a handful of fried onions over it and spread half the rice evenly on top.
Spoon on the vegetable stew, then more fried onions, the chopped cilantro and mint, and cover with the remaining rice.
Spoon over the saffron water, the rose water if using, and the ghee. Cover the dish very tightly with foil and bake at 204C / 400F for 30 minutes. Scatter with almonds to serve.
chefTips: The whole method is built on part-cooking. Chicken to halfway, rice to six minutes, potatoes to just tender — the final thirty minutes of sealed steam finishes all three at once.
Lift the rice out wet. Rice drained until dry has nothing left to steam with and the top layer bakes hard.
Seal the foil properly, right around the rim. Escaped steam is the difference between this working and not.
Marinate overnight if you possibly can. Two hours is the minimum that gets flavour past the skin.
commonMistakes: Boiling the rice to tender, so it is already overcooked before the steaming stage begins.
Draining the rice thoroughly, which is the single commonest cause of a dry biryaani.
Covering the dish loosely, letting the steam escape and leaving the top layer of rice crunchy.
Cooking the chicken through before layering, after which the extra half hour dries it out.
reheating: Cover and warm in a low oven with a splash of water so the rice steams.
healthBenefits: Chicken provides lean protein, niacin and selenium.
Fresh mint, cilantro, ginger and garlic go in raw quantities rather than as a token.
Yogurt contributes calcium and gives the sauce body without cream.
culturalNote: Biryani reached the Somali coast along the same Indian Ocean routes as the samosa and the spice trade, and Somali kitchens made it their own by breaking it into stages. It is party food: a dish made in a wide tray for a table of people rather than a weekday dinner.
